ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, one end of a light spring is tied to a small block of mass m＝1kg, and the other end is fixed to the wall. When the block is at rest on the inclined plane, the angle between the spring and the vertical direction is $37^{\circ}$. It is known that the inclination angle of the inclined plane is $\theta=37^{\circ}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the inclined plane and the small block is $\mu=0.5$, and the inclined plane is fixed and motionless. Suppose that the maximum static friction force between the block and the inclined plane is equal in magnitude to the sliding friction force. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The magnitude of the elastic force of the spring cannot be equal to 3N

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a vertical wall, and on the right side is a fixed inclined plane, with the inclined plane sloping upward to the right; the small block is placed at rest on the inclined plane; one end of the light spring is fixed to the wall on the left side, and the other end is connected to the block, with the direction of the spring pointing from the block to the upper left. The inclination angle of the inclined plane is marked as θ in the figure, and the problem gives θ=37°; the angle between the spring and the vertical direction is also 37°. Therefore, the direction of the spring is consistent with the direction of the normal to the inclined plane, that is, the spring tension is perpendicular to the inclined plane and outward. Reasoning: Assume according to the problem that the elastic force of the spring T=3 N. Take g=10 m/s², m=1 kg, then mg=10 N, sin37°≈0.6, cos37°≈0.8. Along the direction of the inclined plane, the spring has no component, and the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sin37°=10×0.6=6 N; if the block is at rest, the static friction force must be upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude 6 N. In the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane, the component of gravity pressing toward the inclined plane is mg cos37°=10×0.8=8 N, and the normal force N and the spring tension T are both outward along the normal to the inclined plane, so N+T=mg cos37°, that is, N=8-3=5 N. The maximum static friction force fmax=μN=0.5×5=2.5 N. The required static friction force 6 N is greater than the maximum static friction force 2.5 N, so the static friction force is insufficient to maintain equilibrium. Therefore, the magnitude of the elastic force of the spring cannot be equal to 3 N.
